findings.rule: Without `--plan` the command behaves as today.
findings.input: `pandoscope org init some-org --meta M --project app` (no --description, no --approver, no --plan, no --dry-run, no --board-url) on an org with no PROJECT_BOARD_URL and no open project
findings.finding: Today argparse rejects the missing --description/--approver before any forge call, but now the check sits in `_plan`, which runs after `_board` (line 43) has already called `forge.ensure_board` and created a project board in the org, so the refusal arrives only after a side effect.

findings.rule: A file with two code repos and prefixed store names yields a plan whose repos are created, stamped and reconciled under those names (unit level, with the existing fakes).
findings.input: PLAN_FILE in test_a_plan_file_brings_every_repo_it_names: meta, app, helper and no store entries, run with --dry-run
findings.finding: The acceptance test this criterion asks for is missing: the only end-to-end plan-file test has no prefixed stores (e.g. pando-session-memory) and runs with --dry-run, so nothing is created or stamped, and no test checks that the rulesets/credentials confs name the prefixed stores.

findings.rule: The file holds the org, its approvers and one entry per repo: `name`, `purpose`, `kind` (`code`, `docs`, `store`, `plain`), `store` (which store subtemplate, only for `kind: store`), optional `title` (the stamped project name, default the name), `private` (default true), `direct_pushes` (default false).
findings.input: org.yml with `approvers: []` and one `{name: app, kind: code, purpose: p}` entry
findings.finding: read_plan accepts a file with no approvers and stamps gated repos with `agentic_merge_approval_gate: true` and an empty `agentic_merge_approvers`, whereas the same plan built from the flags is refused by default_plan, so the file path yields a plan the flag path cannot.
